comments: Replace with any overall comment, and answer the two questions in the Open questions section of the design. Q1: is it acceptable for the automation to reach Command Center by CSS id, given the application gives that control no accessible name? Q2: in TS-ETA-411-006, does 'each module reached in this plan' mean the five non-Home modules? That reading is the orchestrator's, not something the plan states. Note also that every locator in this design is still MCP_VALIDATION_REQUIRED: approving this gate approves the behaviour, and the locators are proven afterwards at PLAYWRIGHT_VALIDATION.

itemDecisions.comment: Presence of the six named modules, as a data table so the list can change without a step-definition change.
Dashboard icons. Returns Home directly between icons rather than via Command Center, so TS-ETA-411-006 keeps independent evidence.
Navigation menu entries. Kept separate from TS-ETA-411-002 so a working menu cannot mask a broken Dashboard icon.
Preferences offered with Organization and Vault grouped beneath it. Presence only, per AMB-ETA-411-007.
Organization and Vault open their own pages. Arrival asserted on page content because Organization shares an address with the Preferences icon.
Command Center returns Home from each module. Needs a VALIDATED string-selector waiver; the control has no accessible name. See Q1 and Q2.
Unauthenticated visitor refused. The feature has no Background so this scenario genuinely starts unauthenticated. No credential is entered, so no lockout risk.
